item.title: Robinhood Gets Its Day at the Supreme Court Over 2021 IPO Disclosures: Here’s What You Should Know
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court agreed Friday to hear Robinhood Markets Inc.’s NASDAQ:HOOD appeal seeking to end a shareholder lawsuit alleging the brokerage misled investors about its finances and growth ...
item.content:encoded:
News / Benzinga / Robinhood Gets Its Day at the Supreme Court Over 2021 IPO Disclosures: Here’s What You Should Know

Robinhood Gets Its Day at the Supreme Court Over 2021 IPO Disclosures: Here’s What You Should Know 1 min read

HOOD GME DOGEUSD The U.S. Supreme Court agreed Friday to hear Robinhood Markets Inc. ’s HOOD appeal seeking to end a shareholder lawsuit alleging the brokerage misled investors about its finances and growth ahead of its 2021 IPO. The court is expected to rule by the end of June, according to Reuters. Securities Act Claims Center on Meme Stock Disclosures Investors who bought IPO-linked shares sued under the Securities Act of 1933. The law requires companies to disclose accurate information for informed investment decisions. Plaintiffs allege Robinhood failed to disclose that revenue had shifted toward meme stocks like GameStop Corp. GME and the cryptocurrency Dogecoin DOGEUSD . They say that trading frenzy had faded before the July 2021 IPO. They also cite an "exodus of its traditional customers." According to the plaintiffs, Robinhood reported declines in revenue and key performance indicators after its IPO. They allege those declines led to a sharp fall in its stock price. Robinhood has rejected the claims. The company contends its IPO documents made extensive disclosures about future risks and warned of a downturn from the meme-stock and dogecoin-driven trading peaks of early 2021. Robinhood did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment. Lower Courts Split U.S. District Judge Edward Chen dismissed the case in 2024. The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals revived it in 2025, finding Chen applied the wrong legal standards. Robinhood argues the ruling exposes companies to massive liability and risks burying investors in trivial information. Earlier, the Trump administration’s solicitor general, invited by the court to weigh in, recommended that the justices hear the case, but only on when omitting information from an IPO filing can create liability under the Securities Act. Trading Metrics Robinhood has a market capitalization of about $70.11 billion. Over the past 52 weeks, its stock has traded as high as $139.75 and as low as $63.52. Price Action: On Friday, HOOD closed at $77.86, down 4.29%, according to  Benzinga Pro  data. item.description: BTCUSD hovered around $68,700 following Friday’s Wall Street open, rebounding from an earlier dip to roughly $67,500.Key points:US PPI sees largest yearly gain since Q4 2022Data from TradingView ...
item.content:encoded:
News / Cointelegraph / Bitcoin holds below $70K as stocks slip despite a cooler US PPI print

Bitcoin holds below $70K as stocks slip despite a cooler US PPI print 2 min read

BTCUSD Bitcoin BTCUSD hovered around $68,700 following Friday’s Wall Street open, rebounding from an earlier dip to roughly $67,500. Key points: Bitcoin failed to reclaim the $70,000 mark after hitting about $67,500 on Friday, its lowest level since mid-August. The US Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 6.5% year over year in October, 0.1 percentage points below expectations but still the largest increase since November 2022. Rekt Capital warned that a weekly close below $73,000 could mark Bitcoin’s third break of that support level in 2026. US PPI sees largest yearly gain since Q4 2022 Data from TradingView showed BTCUSD down 4% on the day after bouncing from a roughly 12-week low near $67,500.

BTCUSD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView The US Producer Price Index, which tracks changes in the prices domestic producers receive for their goods and services, rose 0.3% month over month and 6.5% year over year in October. Both readings were 0.1 percentage points below market expectations but the annual increase was the largest since November 2022. “Leading the October advance in final demand prices, the index for final demand goods increased 0.5 percent. Prices for final demand services moved up 0.2 percent,” the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported Friday.

US PPI one-month percentage change. Source: BLS Stocks showed little sign of relief at the start of the US trading session, with traders still parsing developments around Nvidia after its co-founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, resigned on Thursday. The S&P 500 was down 1.2% at the time of writing, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index was 1.5% lower.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView The PPI release led markets to slightly adjust expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes. Odds of a minimal 25-basis-point hike at the Fed’s December meeting rose from 85.4% on Thursday to 89.7%, while odds of a larger 50-basis-point move decreased from 14.5% to 10.3%, per data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool.

Fed target-rate probability comparison for the December FOMC meeting. Source: CME Group Economist Robin Brooks described a 25-basis-point hike in December as “all but inevitable.” He argued, however, against a steeper increase, seeing it as ineffective in the face of current inflation drivers: the oil-price spike from the US-Iran war and potential long-term acceleration in underlying inflation. “If high inflation is about the Strait of Hormuz and oil, 75 basis points won’t do anything about that. If the issue is that the pace of underlying inflation has risen, then 75 basis points is much too timid to get this under control,” he wrote. Bitcoin eyes repeat of breakdown that preceded $60,000 drop Crypto trader and analyst Rekt Capital warned that a BTC close below $73,000 on Sunday would mark a support breakdown already seen in 2026. “Last week’s Weekly Candle Closed below 3 Weekly levels,” he wrote on X, referring to $75,000, $76,800 and $78,300. “This Weekly Candle looks set to do something similar. Which is testament to sell-side momentum still gaining and the bears being in control.” After each of the two previous breakdowns, Bitcoin fell to around $60,000.

BTCUSD one-week chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com At $68,700, BTCUSD is down 17.7% in the fourth quarter and 11.2% month to date. The quarterly performance is currently Bitcoin’s second worst on record, data from CoinGlass confirms.

item.description: Bitcoin falls below $68,000 for the first time since August. Traders are watching whether a bounce can reclaim former support at $71,500.📉 Bitcoin breaks below $71,500💸 Liquidations hit the accelera ...
item.content:encoded:
News / TradingView / BTCUSD: Bitcoin Sinks to $67,500, Breaks Rising Channel as Liquidations Surge

BTCUSD: Bitcoin Sinks to $67,500, Breaks Rising Channel as Liquidations Surge 1 min read

BTCUSD Key points: Bitcoin slips through key support Prices shed 9% in two days Liquidations hit $650M in a day

BTCUSD, D1, TradingView Bitcoin falls below $68,000 for the first time since August. Traders are watching whether a bounce can reclaim former support at $71,500. 📉 Bitcoin breaks below $71,500 Bitcoin slid below $68,000 early Friday, with intraday data showing a low of $67,500. The drop took it through $70,000 for the first time since August, extending Thursday’s decline of more than 3% to a two-day dive of 9%. The orange coin is on track to log a sixth straight losing week. The move broke the short-term ascending channel where $71,500 was guarding the support area. With Friday’s selloff breaking that pattern, $71,500 becomes a level where sellers could reappear if Bitcoin bounces. On the flip side, reclaiming $71,500 and holding it on a pullback would give buyers more evidence of a recovery. If $67,500 gives way, the next chart area to watch is around $65,000. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $1.44 billion in net outflows over the five sessions through November 11. The withdrawals show demand through those funds was already weakening before Friday’s break. 💸 Liquidations hit the accelerator More than $650 million in crypto derivatives positions were liquidated in the 24 hours around Thursday’s slide, with bullish bets accounting for most of the total. When exchanges forcibly close leveraged long positions, those orders can add selling pressure to a market that’s already falling. The selloff continued even as US equity futures steadied. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were modestly higher in pre-market deals ahead of the opening bell in New York. That divergence puts more weight on crypto’s own flows and leverage when assessing whether a stock rebound can help.
